job.title: Site Engineer
job.description:
Get closer to the construction and build your career. We’re working with a growing New Zealand civil contractor delivering technically challenging infrastructure projects across Three Waters, pipelines, treatment facilities, structures, piling and specialist civil works.

They self-perform much of their work, with their own crews, plant and engineering capability. For a Site Engineer, that means genuine exposure to how projects are built, rather than simply managing subcontractors.

The role:

Working alongside experienced Project Managers, Engineers and Supervisors,

you’ll take responsibility for packages of work and get involved across:
  • Planning and sequencing site activities
  • QA, ITPs and project documentation
  • Construction methodology and temporary works
  • Programme, productivity and cost monitoring
  • Procurement and subcontractor coordination
  • Working directly with site crews
  • Identifying and solving construction issues
  • Supporting commercial and project reporting
You’ll bring:
  • Strong technical fundamentals
  • A genuine interest in construction methodology
  • Initiative and the ability to think ahead
  • Good communication with both site crews and professional teams
  • A willingness to learn and take feedback
  • Ownership of your work
  • A practical, down-to-earth approach
What we’re looking for Ideally, you’ll have a Civil Engineering degree and some practical construction experience.

Experience across water, wastewater, drainage, pipelines, structures, piling or heavy civil infrastructure would be useful, but attitude and technical ability are just as important.

You’ll enjoy being on site, getting into the detail and understanding how things are actually built. You’ll be proactive, comfortable taking responsibility and keen to keep developing.

Why consider it?

You’ll get exposure to complex projects, experienced technical leaders and considerably more construction responsibility than you might within a heavily subcontracted environment.

If you’re an ambitious Civil Engineer looking to accelerate your development and work on interesting infrastructure projects, get in touch for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Construction Manager
job.description:
This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who wants genuine ownership of a civil operation.

You’ll be leading an established team of around 25 across a mix of water, wastewater, stormwater, utilities and wider civil infrastructure projects. There’s a solid base already in place, but there’s also plenty of opportunity to bring the teams closer together, strengthen how things operate and help shape where the business goes next.

You’ll have the freedom to make decisions, improve things that aren’t working and develop the people around you. For someone who likes the idea of running an operation rather than simply managing a portfolio of projects, there’s a lot to get your teeth into.

The role
Reporting into the senior leadership team, you’ll take responsibility for the performance of the construction operation across multiple projects and teams.

That will include:
  • Leading Project Managers, Supervisors and site teams across multiple civil projects
  • Keeping a close eye on programme, resources, productivity and project performance
  • Owning budgets, forecasting, cost control and commercial outcomes
  • Making sure contracts are being managed properly and risks are picked up early
  • Building strong relationships with clients, consultants and other stakeholders
  • Developing the people underneath you and creating clear accountability across the team
  • Looking at systems, processes and ways of working and improving them where needed
  • Supporting tendering, client relationships and opportunities to grow the operation
  • Maintaining strong safety, quality and environmental standards
Who are we looking for?
You could already be operating as a Construction Manager, or you may be a strong Senior Project Manager, Contracts Manager or operational leader who is ready to take on a broader business.

You’ll need a solid civil construction background and experience leading multiple projects and people. Three Waters experience would be particularly useful, although we’re open to broader civil infrastructure backgrounds where the fundamentals are strong.

You’ll understand the commercial side of construction as well as delivery. Contracts, margins, forecasting, programming and resource planning shouldn’t be things that sit solely with someone else.

The person behind the experience matters too.

We’re looking for someone who takes ownership, works hard and has good judgement. You’ll be comfortable making decisions independently, but equally comfortable asking questions, listening to your team and bringing people with you when things need to change.

You don’t need to arrive with all the answers. You do need to be curious enough to work out what could be better and have the drive to do something about it.

Why consider it?
The attraction here is the amount of influence you can have. This is a smaller operation where you’ll be close to the people doing the work and close to the people making the decisions. Good ideas can actually be acted on.

There are established clients, an experienced team and a broad portfolio of civil work already in place, but there is also genuine scope to improve the operation and help build what comes next.

If you’ve spent time in a larger contractor and like the idea of having more ownership, or you’re already running teams and want a role with broader operational responsibility, it’s worth a conversation.

You don’t need to be actively looking. If this has caught your attention, get in touch with Ginny Ryder at RWR Construction for a confidential chat.

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
About the Company:

We're working with one of New Zealand's leading specialists in water treatment and process infrastructure. They deliver complex design and build projects across municipal and industrial sectors, combining in-house engineering, fabrication, construction and commissioning under one roof.

With around 100 staff, this business has built an outstanding reputation delivering complex water infrastructure projects nationwide.
The culture is collaborative, practical and hands on. People are trusted to make decisions, take ownership and contribute to the continued growth of the business.

Internal development is genuinely encouraged, with many senior leaders having progressed through the organisation.

As demand continues to grow, they're looking for a Project Manager who can take ownership of multidisciplinary projects from early design coordination through to successful delivery on site.

You'll be involved from the earliest stages of a project, coordinating consultants, working alongside process and mechanical engineers, managing civil and building interfaces, and ensuring projects are delivered safely, commercially and to programme.

Projects typically range from around $500k through to well into the multi million dollar range and are located throughout New Zealand.

You'll be responsible for:
  • Managing projects from design through to construction and commissioning
  • Coordinating civil, structural, mechanical, electrical and process disciplines
  • Managing external consultants and subcontractors
  • Working closely with internal engineering and fabrication teams
  • Overseeing programme, commercial performance and client relationships
  • Travelling to project sites throughout New Zealand as required, typically around one week per month
About You:

We're open on background, but you'll ideally bring experience delivering multidisciplinary infrastructure or industrial projects.

You might come from:
  • Three Waters
  • Water or wastewater treatment
  • Industrial or process plants
  • Mechanical services
  • Civil infrastructure
  • Heavy industrial construction
More importantly, you'll have:
  • Proven experience managing projects from design through to completion
  • Strong understanding of coordinating multiple disciplines
  • Confidence managing subcontractors and consultants
  • Excellent communication and client management skills
  • Commercial awareness and programme management capability
  • The ability to work autonomously and take ownership
What's on Offer:
  • Salary circa $150,000-$170,000 depending on experience
  • Work on technically interesting, multidisciplinary projects
  • National project exposure across New Zealand
  • Genuine autonomy and ownership
  • Strong pipeline of secured work
  • Long-term career development within a growing organisation
  • Supportive, high-performing team culture
If you're looking for a Project Management role where you'll be involved in far more than simply delivering construction, we'd love to have a confidential chat.

Apply now or contact Alex on 027 370 7011 or alexb@rwrconstruction.co.nz

job.title: Quantity Surveyor
job.description:
Looking for more than just another Quantity Surveying role?

Our client is a well-established residential builder with an exciting pipeline of work and a reputation for delivering quality homes across the Northland. Due to continued growth, they're looking to add an experienced Quantity Surveyor to their team.

This is a broad role where you'll be involved from the early pricing stages through to project completion, working alongside experienced estimators, project managers and operational leaders on a diverse range of residential projects.
  
You'll play a key role in the commercial delivery of residential construction projects, with responsibilities including:
  • Preparing estimates and detailed cost plans.
  • Procurement and subcontractor engagement.
  • Producing purchase orders and managing budgets.
  • Contract administration and project cost control.
  • Managing variations and payment claims.
  • Supporting Project Managers throughout construction.
  • Liaising with clients, consultants, suppliers and subcontractors.
  • Contributing to value engineering and commercial decision-making.
About You.

We're looking for someone who has:
  • Residential Quantity Surveying experience in New Zealand (group housing experience preferred).
  • Strong estimating and post-contract QS capability.
  • Excellent commercial judgement and attention to detail.
  • The ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
  • A collaborative, solutions-focused approach.
What's on Offer?
  • Join a growing business with a strong pipeline of work.
  • Variety across first-home builds, architectural homes and multi-home developments.
  • Work alongside an experienced commercial and construction team.
  • Genuine opportunities to broaden your experience and contribute commercially.
  • Supportive leadership with ongoing mentoring and career development.
  • Competitive salary package based on experience.
If you're looking for a role that combines technical Quantity Surveying with genuine variety, experienced leadership and long-term career growth, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: New Home Consultant
job.description:
New Home Sales Consultant | Bay of Plenty

If you're good at sales, enjoy building relationships and would rather create opportunities than wait for the phone to ring, this could be a very good move.
  
We're working with an established residential building business looking to add an experienced sales professional to its New Home Consultant team. The role will be based in Rotorua, representing the business locally, with the wider team and head office based in Tauranga.

This isn't simply about sitting in a show home and dealing with incoming enquiries. You'll have the backing of an established national brand, marketing support and a strong local business, but you'll also be expected to get out into the market and create your own opportunities.

That could mean building relationships with landowners, developers, agents and other local contacts, getting involved in the community, following up leads, networking and finding opportunities before they necessarily land on your desk.
Once you've got a client engaged, you'll work with them through the early stages of their new home journey. You'll understand what they're trying to achieve, work through land and build options, help shape the right solution and keep the relationship moving through to contract.

We're reasonably open on where your experience has come from. New home sales experience would obviously translate well, but we're equally interested in people from other sales environments who can demonstrate a genuine track record of business development, prospecting and generating their own pipeline.

You'll need to be comfortable starting conversations, following up consistently and asking for the business. Just as importantly, you need to be someone clients trust with what is often one of the biggest financial decisions they'll make.

An understanding of residential construction, property or development would be useful, but it isn't necessarily the deciding factor. Sales capability, commercial drive and your ability to build relationships will carry plenty of weight.

You'll be joining an experienced, down-to-earth team with plenty happening across the wider Bay of Plenty market. There's good support around you, but also enough autonomy to get out there and build something for yourself.

If you've got a proven sales background in New Zealand and the idea of moving into new homes appeals, we'd be keen to have a conversation.

job.title: New Home Sales Consultant
job.description:
New Home Sales Consultant | Northland
 
If you're a proven salesperson who enjoys getting out, meeting people and creating your own opportunities, this could be a great move into the new home market.

We're working with an established residential building business looking to add a New Home Consultant to its Northland team. Based from the Ruakākā office, you'll look after the territory extending north through Whangārei and up towards Kerikeri, building relationships, developing your network and generating new business along the way.

You'll have the backing of a recognised national building brand and an experienced local team, but this isn't a role where you'll simply sit back and wait for enquiries to arrive. There will be leads and marketing support, but a big part of your success will come from getting out into the market and creating your own pipeline.

That could mean developing relationships with agents, developers, landowners and other local contacts, attending events, following up opportunities and becoming genuinely well connected across the local property and building market.

Once you've got a client engaged, you'll guide them through the new home sales process. You'll understand what they're trying to achieve, work through land and build options, bring the right people into the conversation and keep things moving towards contract.

New home sales experience would obviously be valuable, but it isn't the only background we're interested in. We're open to strong salespeople from property, automotive, building products or other relationship-led sales environments where you've been responsible for finding and converting your own business.

What matters is that you can demonstrate a genuine track record in sales and business development. You'll be comfortable prospecting, starting conversations, following up consistently and asking for the business. You'll understand that building a pipeline takes time and be motivated enough to keep creating opportunities rather than relying solely on inbound leads.

Personality matters too. We're looking for someone confident, personable and commercially driven who genuinely enjoys dealing with people. Someone who can build trust quickly, have a bit of fun along the way and develop relationships that last beyond a single sale.

An understanding of construction, property or development would be useful, but you don't need to know everything on day one. You'll have experienced people around you, along with the systems and support of an established building brand.

If you've got the sales ability, drive and personality to build a strong presence, we'd be keen to hear from you.

Apply now or contact Maximilian at RWR Construction for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Site Manager
job.description:
Good Site Managers know when to plan, when to push, and when to get out on site and sort the thing that’s holding everyone up. That’s the balance this role needs.

We’re working with a Wellington construction business delivering commercial projects where the expectation is straightforward: take ownership of the site, keep the programme moving, communicate well, and deal with issues before they become bigger ones.

The role will suit someone who is commercially experienced, practical in their approach, and comfortable working with a bit of autonomy.

The role
You’ll take responsibility for the day-to-day running of commercial construction sites and work closely with the wider project team to keep programme, quality and delivery on track.

That includes:
  • coordinating trades and site activity
  • managing short-term programmes and sequencing
  • staying on top of drawings, RFIs and site issues
  • keeping quality and safety where they need to be
  • communicating with clients, consultants and project teams
  • maintaining the documentation that keeps the job under control
  • identifying issues early and working through them
  • carrying the site through to completion and handover
What they’re looking for
You’ll need solid commercial construction experience and enough exposure to larger, structured projects that client meetings, programmes and multiple work fronts feel normal.

Tier 2 or Tier 1 experience would be useful, but it doesn’t need to define your whole career. A trade background is helpful, but the bigger thing is balance.
They don’t want someone who can only do the practical side, and they don’t want someone who only manages from behind a screen. You need to be able to do both.
  • Practical enough to understand what’s happening on site.
  • Organised enough to stay ahead of programme.
  • Confident enough to deal with clients.
  • And proactive enough to keep things moving when the answer isn’t immediately obvious.
The environment
The business is growing, the work is varied, and the way they operate is relatively unbureaucratic. People who do well are generally positive, accountable and low ego. You’ll have support around you, but you’ll also be trusted to get on with the job.

If you like a highly prescribed environment with a process for everything, this probably won’t be the right fit. If you like being given responsibility, working things out, and being part of a team that gets stuck in, it could be a very good one.

Interested? We’re less interested in a polished CV than we are in understanding what you’ve actually run. If you’ve delivered commercial sites, managed programme and trades, dealt directly with clients, and can talk honestly about the problems you’ve had to solve along the way, we’d be keen to hear from you.

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
RWR Construction has partnered with a specialist infrastructure contractor who is looking for a Project Manager to help deliver a range of stormwater, wastewater and drainage projects across Auckland and the North Island.

Projects include both new builds & maintenance projects.

You’ll manage multiple small to medium projects at various stages from planning through to completion, coordinating crews, subcontractors and suppliers while working directly with clients.

This role suits someone who enjoys running multiple projects end-to-end, rather than being responsible for a small piece of a large project.

This is a key position for our client, you will be part of the senior leadership team & reporting into the directors.

Key responsibilities:
  • Manage multiple infrastructure projects simultaneously
  • Coordinate site crews, subcontractors and suppliers
  • Interface directly with clients and consultants
  • Manage variations, commercial outcomes and contracts
  • Plan works, resources and materials
  • Troubleshoot technical issues onsite
  • Support design-build solutions where required
Projects include:
  • Stormwater and wastewater infrastructure
  • Pump stations and drainage systems
  • Septic and wastewater installations
  • Civil works associated with water infrastructure
About You:
  • 5+ years experience in civil or infrastructure construction
  • Experience with drainage, stormwater or wastewater projects
  • Engineering qualification, Civil or Mechanical preferred
  • Strong communication and practical problem-solving skills
  • Comfortable managing multiple projects and site teams
If you tick the above boxes & would like to find out more, click apply now or reach out to Alex on 027 370 7011 or alexb@rwrconstruction.co.nz

job.title: Operations Manager
job.description:
The Opportunity:

A growing specialist contractor operating across construction, civil infrastructure and asset maintenance is looking for an experienced Operations Manager to take ownership of its operational delivery function.
Reporting to the General Manager and sitting on the Senior Leadership Team, this role will work closely with the Commercial Manager and take responsibility for projects from contract award through planning, mobilisation, delivery, claims and closeout.

This is an Operations Manager role, not a Project Manager stepping up. The focus is on leading managers, driving operational performance and ensuring the people, resources and systems across the business are working together effectively.

The business has a strong pipeline of work and national growth ambitions. This person will play a key role in building the operational capability required to support that growth.

** Please note, this position is based in the Waikato and relocation is required **

Key Responsibilities:
  • Own operational delivery across multiple construction and infrastructure workstreams.
  • Lead approximately five direct reports across project delivery, HSEQ, scheduling/administration and plant and equipment maintenance.
  • Take ownership of operational P&L performance, including productivity, cost control, forecasting and resource utilisation.
  • Manage the handover from commercial/pre-construction through planning, mobilisation, delivery and closeout.
  • Oversee programming, labour, plant and resource allocation across multiple concurrent projects.
  • Improve planning, communication, accountability and follow-through across the delivery teams.
  • Set clear expectations for operational managers and hold them accountable for performance.
  • Develop the capability of the managers and supervisors underneath the role.
  • Maintain oversight of project commercials, including claims, variations and contractual obligations.
  • Ensure project teams capture accurate and timely information to support claims and invoicing.
  • Work closely with the Commercial Manager on contractual and commercial issues throughout delivery.
  • Provide leadership oversight across HSEQ, QA, operational compliance and plant.
  • Identify operational risks, capability gaps and performance issues and address them early.
  • Build stronger systems and processes to support a growing national operation.
  • Contribute to business planning and strategic decision-making as part of the Senior Leadership Team.
Key Performance Indicators:
  • Project delivery against programme, budget, quality and client expectations.
  • Operational margin and overall P&L performance.
  • Labour utilisation, productivity and effective resource allocation.
  • Accuracy and timeliness of claims, variations and invoicing information.
  • Forward planning of labour, plant and project requirements.
  • HSEQ and quality performance.
  • Accountability and performance across the operational management team.Own operations, lead the team and drive performance for a growing specialist contractor with a strong national pipeline.
  • Development and capability of managers and supervisors.
  • Client delivery, repeat business and operational service levels.
  • Development of scalable systems and operational capability as the business grows.
What We're Looking For:

We are looking for an established Operations Manager with experience in construction, civil infrastructure, specialist contracting or a similar project led environment.

You will have proven experience leading managers and operational teams, with genuine responsibility for P&L and business performance.

Strong construction and commercial knowledge is essential, including an understanding of NZS 3910, claims, variations, programming and project financials.

You don't need to be the technical specialist; the priority is your ability to lead people, understand performance and get the best out of the resources around you.

Experience across both construction projects and asset maintenance or facilities environments would be advantageous.

You'll need to be comfortable entering a business where there is an opportunity to strengthen operational performance. Initially, that will mean getting into the detail, setting expectations and creating accountability before progressively empowering the team underneath you.

The role is predominantly office based in Hamilton, with site involvement and national travel when senior operational support is required.

For the right person, there is significant scope to grow with the business and potentially progress into broader business leadership over time.

If you tick the above boxes & would like to find out more, apply today or reach out to Alex on 027 370 7011 or alexb@rwrconstruction.co.nz

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
Join an established New Zealand civil construction business with more than 30+ years of industry experience and a strong pipeline of infrastructure work.

Specialising in piling, precast concrete, retaining walls and bridge construction, the business delivers technically challenging projects throughout New Zealand. This is an opportunity to join a stable contractor, take ownership of multiple projects and work with an experienced civil team.

**Please note, this role is based in the Hawkes Bay & relocation is required**

Why Join?
  • Secure, long-term employment
  • Strong pipeline of civil and infrastructure projects
  • Projects valued up to $5 million
  • Career development and upskilling opportunities
  • Supportive, practical team culture
  • Company vehicle, phone and laptop
The Role Reporting to the Civil Manager, you will manage civil construction projects from planning through to completion, ensuring they are delivered safely, on time, within scope and within budget.

This position involves operational delivery, commercial management, client communication and team leadership. You may oversee several projects concurrently, so strong organisation, commercial awareness and the ability to prioritise are essential.

The position is permanently based in Hastings. Candidates currently living elsewhere must be willing to relocate to Hawke’s Bay. This is not a FIFO opportunity.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Manage civil projects valued up to $5 million
  • Lead, support and mentor civil delivery teams
  • Develop and manage project programmes, budgets and resources
  • Coordinate with clients, site teams and production teams
  • Monitor project costs, financial performance and variations
  • Oversee contractual, quality assurance and reporting requirements
  • Maintain accurate project documentation and progress updates
  • Ensure health and safety standards are consistently maintained
  • Assist with tenders, pricing, quotes and client submissions
  • Participate in management, project and toolbox meetings
  • Maintain strong client relationships throughout delivery
Skills and Experience You will ideally bring:
  • At least five years’ Project Management experience in New Zealand civil construction
  • Experience delivering piling, deep foundations, structures, bridges or retaining-wall projects
  • Strong knowledge of NZS 3910 and NZS 3916 contracts
  • Experience with cost control, financial reporting and pricing variations
  • Sound knowledge of civil construction methods, procedures and equipment
  • Strong planning, operational and organisational skills
  • The ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • A practical and confident leadership style
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making ability
  • The ability to mentor others and contribute to a high-performing team
  • A strong understanding of health and safety requirements
  • A valid New Zealand driver licence
  • The legal right to work in New Zealand
Position Details:
  • Based in Hastings, Hawke’s Bay
  • Permanent relocation to Hawke’s Bay is required
  • Full-time, permanent position
  • Occasional travel based on project requirements
  • Company vehicle, phone and laptop provided
If you are an experienced Civil Project Manager looking for long term stability, technical project variety and the opportunity to make a genuine impact within a well established contractor, apply now or reach out to Alex on 027 370 7011 or alexb@rwrconstruction.co.nz
